methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in distributed AI literacy outside major metros, creating potential peer learning networks that could spread deep capability through Southwest Virginia's workforce beyond platform-level adoption.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability building explicitly targeting equity gaps, offering a distributed peer-learning pathway that could build deep fluency rather than shallow platform consumption if sustained.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National
signals.signal_reading: Children's National-Virginia Tech partnership concentrates specialized pediatric AI expertise between two elite institutions, deepening capability in specific nodes while the collaboration structure reinforces hub-and-spoke patterns rather than distributing know-how to community providers.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: This commentary explicitly names data center concentration in NoVA as infrastructure that increases urban-rural divide, signaling how AI's physical footprint may entrench advantages without generating distributed capability or economic spillover to non-metro regions.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's new AI minor creates curriculum infrastructure for deep technical capability in the New River Valley, potentially seeding peer networks among graduates who could distribute expertise through regional employers rather than immediately migrating to NoVA.
